newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. force in S. Lebanon renewed for six months.
newsitem.headline: U.N. force in S. Lebanon renewed for six months.

text.p: The Security Council on Tuesday unanimously approved a six-month renewal, until July 31, of the U.N. peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon.

The 4,500-member U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) was established in 1978 to restore the Lebanese government's authority over the region after an Israeli incursion against Palestinian guerrillas.

After Israel withdrew its troops following a 1982 invasion, it retained a so-called security zone along the Lebanese side of the border, aided by its allies of the South Lebanon Army militia, to block attacks against northern Israel. This has resulted in sporadic clashes mainly with Iranian-backed guerrillas.
The resolution renewing UNIFIL's mandate condemned "all acts of violence committed in particular against the force" and urged the parties to end them.
It also reiterated the council's strong support for Lebanon's territorial integrity, sovereignty and political independence and again said the force should fully implement its mandate.
The resolution encouraged "further efficiency and savings" provided they did not affect UNIFIL's operational capacity.
Secretary-General Kofi Annan drew attention in a recent report to unpaid assessments by U.N. members of $177 million for the upkeep of the force.

UNIFIL, which costs about $125 million a year, comprises contingents from Estonia, Fiji, Finland, France, Ghana, Ireland, Italy, Nepal, Norway and Poland. It is commanded by Major-General Stanislaw Wozniak of Poland.
